column1: # *** WHAT A SECOND INDEX FOUND IN ONE DAY. 11 October 2026. ***
# FamilySearch has TWO indexes and this archive had been using one of them.
#   The RECORD INDEX is built by transcribing entries into fields. It catalogues PRINCIPALS and
#   PARENTS, and it loses everyone else on the page - witnesses, godparents, deponents, neighbours.
#   The FULL-TEXT CORPUS is built by reading the page image. It finds a name anywhere it appears.
# *** THREE OF THIS ARCHIVE'S STANDING NULLS HAD BEEN TESTED ONLY IN THE FIRST ***, and written up
# as facts about FamilySearch. They were facts about one of its two indexes. Everything below came
# out of a single day of asking the other one.
*** A marriage declared unfindable, found by one phrase search. *** Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Cordon, Montevideo, *** 28 DECEMBER 1871 ***. Image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-B3DF-C.
column2: *** "D. ALEJANDRO MAXIMO SERENA, soltero, natural de Montevideo, hijo de D. AVELINO y de Dona AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, con Dona ELISA VILLADEMOROS, del mismo estado y oriundez, HIJA DE LOS FINADOS D. PEDRO y Dona ANGELICA VILLADEMOROS." *** Two conciliar banns dispensed. Witnesses *** Dr D. JOAQUIN REQUENA *** and *** DONA AMBROSIA T. DE SERENA *** - the groom's own mother.
column3: Work-list row 185 had twice concluded this act "must be walked by image". *** IT WAS IN THE OTHER INDEX ALL ALONG. *** It gives his full name - the "M." is *** MAXIMO *** - and names his parents independently of the enrolment cards. *** AND ITS LAST CLAUSE PAYS FOR THE WHOLE SEARCH: *** Celedonia Villademoros is the daughter of Pedro Villademoros and Angelica Mendez, so *** ELISA AND CELEDONIA ARE SISTERS ***, a reading carried as "probably" since September. Both grooms are sons of Avelino Lerena Fernandez and Ambrosia Traibel. *** TWO LERENA BROTHERS MARRIED TWO VILLADEMOROS SISTERS ***, which makes the Lerena Villademoros cousins *** DOUBLE FIRST COUSINS *** - the same structure found at Trinidad the same day, a generation earlier and in another department. It also forces the 1873 godmother to be a THIRD sister, since the mother was already dead. *** WHAT IT DOES NOT GIVE IS HIS AGE ***, which is what the row wanted most, and that question stays open.

column1: *** The apex ancestor speaks, for the first time in this archive's life. *** Catedral Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe, Canelones - Religious Marriage Investigation Files 1776-1806, the expediente of Florentino Gomez. Images 340-341 of 457, DGS 008166573 item 8.
column2: *** "Florentino Gomez presento por testigo en esta Vicaria a SANCHO LLERENA, a quien se le recibio juramento ... el compareciente dijo: Que con motivo de haber andado el declarante EN LA LINEA DE VITORIA algunos anos, que conocio en aquel parage a Florentino Gonzalez ..." *** and, on the next frame, *** "... que dijo NO SABER ESCRIVIR, y la firmo su merced conmigo el presente Notario." ***
column3: Every other record of Sancho holds him as a father, a father of the bride, a spouse or an "other" - because the record index catalogues principals and parents and he was neither. *** HERE HE IS A SWORN WITNESS DEPOSING IN THE FIRST PERSON. *** This archive has held him since its first week and had never known anything about the man rather than his relationships. Now: a man who had spent years on a frontier line, who was trusted to swear to another man's freedom to marry, and *** WHO COULD NOT SIGN HIS OWN NAME ***. *** HIS AGE IS NOT ON THE ACT *** - the witness before him gives one, so the file states ages when it has them, and for Sancho it does not. *** WHAT "LA LINEA DE VITORIA" MEANS IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND IS NOT GUESSED: *** a "linea" in the Rio de la Plata is ordinarily a military frontier, and Vitoria is also a Basque city and a common Brazilian and Spanish place name. The open question on whether this family is Basque or Extremaduran is *** NOT *** advanced by it.

column1: *** A man of this name holding office, with a signature. *** Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City - Probate Estate Case Files, *** 1800 ***. Image ark 3:1:3QHV-P3FJ-Z942, item 12 of 249 images.
column2: *** "Asi lo proveyo, y firmo Don RAMON LERENA, ALCALDE DE LA SANTA HERMANDAD DEL PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO, a seis dias del mes de Noviembre del ano mil ochocientos. RAMON LERENA." *** He notifies the widow *** DONA CELESTINA GONZALEZ *** and certifies *** "A FALTA DE ESCRIBANO PUBLICO NI REAL, POR NO HABERLO EN ESTA JURISDICCION." ***
column3: A rural magistrate of a district with *** no notary in it at all ***, which says something plain about how thinly governed that country was. *** AND HE WROTE: he signs twice *** - where Sancho Llerena, nine years earlier, could not. Two men of this family on either side of that line, and the archive now has both. *** AND THE PLACE IS NOW PROVED, BY THE COURT ITSELF. *** Hours after this row first read "indicated, not proved", the providencia that started the business was found at image 22 and it addresses *** "El Alcalde de la Santa Hermandad del PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO, EN LA OTRA BANDA ORIENTAL de este [Rio]" *** - so the Rosario is *** URUGUAYAN ***. And the widow is *** "Dona CELESTINA GONZALEZ, VECINA DEL COLLA" ***. *** THIS REGISTER HAS CALLED HIM "RAMON LERENA OF ROSARIO-COLLA" SINCE ITS EARLY WEEKS, ON THE STRENGTH OF A KINSHIP DIAGRAM DRAWN IN 1858. THE COURT PUTS HIM IN EXACTLY THAT PLACE, HOLDING OFFICE, IN 1800. *** *** WHAT HE WAS DOING: *** JOSE RIERA, Juez de Menores of Buenos Aires, ordered him to inventory the estate of DON CLEMENTE GARCIA because the widow was RESISTING it, having "pasado a segundas nupcias, teniendo hijo menor". Ramon notified her on 14 October 1800 *** in the presence of her second husband ***, began at "la nominada Villa del Rosario" on the 15th, decreed on 6 November, returned on the 11th with three men, and sat through the appraisal on the 12th. *** FIVE WEEKS OF ONE MAN'S WORK, RECOVERED FROM A FILE INDEXED UNDER ANOTHER FAMILY'S NAME. *** *** AN OBSERVATION THAT IS NOT AN ARGUMENT: the 1858 diagram puts RAMON LERENA and MARIA GONZALEZ at the apex, and the woman at the centre of this file is a GONZALEZ of the Colla. Gonzalez is among the commonest surnames in the Rio de la Plata and NO CONNECTION IS CLAIMED. ***

column1: *** A passenger-list name becomes a family, almost. *** Parroquia y Vicaria de San Jose de Flores, Buenos Aires - baptism *** No. 461 of 10 November 1912 ***. Image ark 3:1:939D-G6VB-K.
column2: *** "Bautizo solemnemente ... a JUANA, que nacio el dia veinte y cinco de Junio ... hija legitima de D. ELOY LERENA, natural de ESPANA, de veinte y seis anos de edad, y de Dona FELISA LERENA, natural de Espana, de veinte y un anos de edad." *** Godparents *** GREGORIO LERENA *** and *** ROSA DEFENARI ***.
column3: *** BOTH PARENTS ARE LERENAS *** - a fifth Lerena-married-a-Lerena couple here, and the first that is Spanish and urban rather than Uruguayan and rural, which is worth noticing before anyone explains the pattern by the smallness of a country parish. *** AND IT WAS NOT MERGED WITH THE PASSENGER LISTS, WHICH IS THE POINT. *** This archive holds a Felisa and a Gregorio Lerena who landed together off the INDIANA from Barcelona on 7 December 1911 and nothing else whatever about either. A Felisa and a Gregorio stand in this parish eleven months later. *** THE ARITHMETIC IS NOT CLEAN: *** the act makes Felisa twenty-one, so born about 1891, where the 1911 list says 1893 - and the archive's OTHER Felisa, who arrived in 1923, is recorded 1891 exactly. *** AND THE ROLES DO NOT LINE UP: *** the 1911 pair travelled TOGETHER, but here Gregorio is only the godfather and the husband is ELOY, who is on no passenger list held here.

column1: *** A null that got stronger, and a null the control EXPLAINED. *** Two of this archive's standing conclusions, re-tested in the second index on the same day.
column2: *** JOSE LORETO LERENA: *** "Loreto Lerena" returns three hits and not one is Uruguayan. The control was run *** AFTER *** the null - "Ambrosia Traibel" returns three pages including Montevideo parish records - so the instrument demonstrably reaches these registers. *** PABLO ARMANDO LERENA: *** returns ZERO. Control after: "Rosario de Santa Fe" returns 245 pages, so the corpus works and reaches *** ARGENTINA ***.
column3: *** THE FIRST NULL IS NOW MUCH STRONGER: *** it holds in two independent indexes, where before it held in one. *** THE SECOND IS NOT A NULL ABOUT THE RECORD AT ALL. *** The Argentine holdings the corpus surfaces are *** Buenos Aires probate, notarial and ship files - and there is NO SANTA FE COLLECTION IN IT ***. So the zero is about COVERAGE and says nothing whatever about whether the Rosario baptism exists. *** WITHOUT THE CONTROL IT COULD HAVE BEEN WRITTEN UP AS A THIRD INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION THAT THE ACT IS NOT THERE *** - which is exactly the error this archive made in the other direction the same morning, arguing in public for a surname nobody had checked.

column1: *** THE OLDEST LERENA THIS ARCHIVE CAN NAME, SIX YEARS OLDER THAN THIS MORNING - AND IN A DIFFERENT JOB. *** Two more probate files from the Buenos Aires court, 1794 and 1796, both reached by paging past the first page of results.
column2: *** 1794, Garcia estate: *** "caminamos a la ESTANCIA del finado Don CLEMENTE GARCIA, y llegados que fuimos parecieron ante mi y testigos Don GERONIMO ALONSO y Don RAMON LERENA, SUJETOS NOMBRADOS POR LA VIUDA PARA CONTAR Y TASAR EL GANADO Y CABALLOS de dicha Estancia... prestaron separadamente cada cual su JURAMENTO... lo que firmaron conmigo y testigos A FALTA DE ESCRIBANO." Signed *** Ramon Lerena ***, with GUILLERMO HURTADO DE VILLAGOMEZ, LORENZO MARTINEZ DE OLALLA, FULGENCIO DE LOS SANTOS and GERONIMO ALONSO. *** 1796, Chabo estate: *** "lo proveyo, mando y firmo *** D. RAMON LERENA, ALCALDE DE LA SANTA HERMANDAD DEL PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO ***... a veintiocho dias del mes de OCTUBRE DE MIL SETECIENTOS NOVENTA Y SEIS anos."
column3: *** 1794, 1796, 1800 - AND THE 1794 ENTRY IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, BECAUSE HE IS NOT THE MAGISTRATE IN IT. *** He is a private man whom a widow picks, swears in and trusts to count the cattle and horses her son will inherit; two years later he is the magistrate of that district, and six years after that he is the magistrate sent back to the same estate to make her account for it. *** THIS ARCHIVE NOW HOLDS A CAREER, WHICH IS MORE THAN IT HOLDS FOR ANY OTHER LERENA BEFORE 1850 *** - no birth, no marriage, no death, but a competence (livestock), a standing (sworn appraiser), and a rise to office. It also moves CLEMENTE GARCIA'S DEATH BACK TO BEFORE 1794 and adds an *** ESTANCIA *** to the shop and the mill. *** AND IT DRAWS THE LINE THIS ARCHIVE WROTE YESTERDAY: *** the Chabo household is NOT admitted - he was only the official there - while the Garcia household is, because in 1794 the widow engaged him personally. *** THE RULE AND ITS BOUNDARY, TESTED ON THE SAME MAN IN TWO ROLES ON ONE DAY. ***

column1: *** A LERENA WHO MARRIED A LERENA - DOCUMENTED, AND NOT IN SOUTH AMERICA. *** The Spanish consulate at Buenos Aires kept notarial registers of its own, and this archive had never opened one.
column2: *** Consulado de Espana en Buenos Aires, 14 November 1900, escritura No. 368: *** "comparecieron los hermanos Don Prudencio Benito y Don JUAN JOSE LERENA Y LERENA, mayores de edad, solteros, dependientes, NATURALES DE NAVARRETE, PROVINCIA DE LOGRONO, vecinos de esta Capital e inscritos en este Consulado... con los numeros novecientos cincuenta y novecientos cincuenta y uno... que confieren poder general y bastante en derecho a SU MADRE DONA ISABELA LORENA Y BASARAN, VIUDA, y a SU HERMANO DON JOSE DOLORES LEERENA Y LERENA, CASADO Y PROPIETARIO, los dos vecinos de Navarrete... para administrar los bienes que los dicentes poseen en Espana."
column3: *** WHAT IT CHANGES IS SMALLER THAN THIS ARCHIVE FIRST WROTE, AND THE FIRST VERSION STOOD FOR TWENTY MINUTES. *** It said a Lerena marrying a Lerena had been the easiest thing on Pablo Armando's 1908 card to dismiss as a clerk writing the surname twice, and that this household answered it. *** THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY HERE SIX TIMES OVER: *** the Trinidad couples of 1894 and 1913, the 1911 dispensation, Alejandro, and Eloy x Felisa Lerena baptising a daughter at San Jose de Flores in 1912 - that last one found the same morning, in this same table. *** SO WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW: *** the first such household *** OUTSIDE SOUTH AMERICA ***; the first in which the children carry the name *** DOUBLED AS A SURNAME OF RECORD ***, signing themselves 'Lerena y Lerena' rather than merely having two Lerena parents; and the first time the practice has *** A PLACE ON A MAP - Navarrete, Logrono - whose parish registers can be opened. *** It also probably identifies a row that has sat here as four bare facts: 'Juan Jose LERENA, b.1876, Logrono, soltero, comercio', landed 1920, 1928, 1929. *** NOT MERGED - CEMLA gives a province, the act gives a village. *** And it opens a source class this archive had never touched: *** the Spanish consulate's own notarial register ***, which records a Spaniard's VILLAGE and his consular roll number where an Argentine civil act gives neither.
